reviews.reasoning: Span re-derived and not contested: web:Ps.18.43-Ps.18.48 tiles cleanly against both witnesses (oshb:Ps.18.44-Ps.18.49; Ps 18 is shift+1 per web_mt_offset_map.json), the row crosses no psalm boundary, and the psalm-tail shape it proposes — dominion, acclamation, then the vow that opens the next row — is defensible. The selah note is true and span-scoped: pmarks_Ps.json carries 0 selah occurrences anywhere in Ps 18, and mark absence is never counterevidence here. All 3 WEB quotations are verbatim against verse_map_web at web:Ps.18.43, web:Ps.18.46 and web:Ps.18.48. What fails is the discriminator the row states for its internal grouping: it characterises web:Ps.18.46-Ps.18.48 as 'third-person epithets for Yahweh rather than second-person address', but the verse it names as the cluster's close carries two 2ms verbs addressed to God — and the row's own quotation of that verse contains one of them. The third-person description is accurate for the 2 verses web:Ps.18.46-Ps.18.47 only, and the person contrast cannot separate the acclamation from the dominion verses because those are 2ms as well. Confidence 'medium' is appropriately calibrated and the rejected_alternative names a real rival, so the repair is to the warrant's stated feature, not to the seam.

challenges.claim: The row's stated discriminator for the acclamation cluster — third-person epithets 'rather than second-person address' — is false at the verse the row names as that cluster's close, and the same feature fails to distinguish the cluster from the dominion verses it is contrasted with.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.18.49 = web:Ps.18.48 carries two second-person (2ms) verbs with 1cs object suffixes: תְּרוֹמְמֵ֑נִי and תַּצִּילֵֽנִי (collate.py: byte tier at that ref for both). WEB renders them inside the very clause the row quotes: “Yes, you lift me up above those who rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.” (web:Ps.18.48). The contrast also fails on the other side of the seam it draws: the dominion verses open with 2ms forms תְּפַלְּטֵנִי֮ and תְּ֭שִׂימֵנִי at oshb:Ps.18.44 = web:Ps.18.43, rendered “You have delivered me from the strivings of the people. You have made me the head of the nations.” (web:Ps.18.43). Third-person doxological forms are real but confined to two verses — וּבָר֣וּךְ and וְ֝יָר֗וּם at oshb:Ps.18.47 = web:Ps.18.46, הָאֵ֗ל הַנּוֹתֵ֣ן at oshb:Ps.18.48 = web:Ps.18.47 (byte tier) — so the accurate statement covers web:Ps.18.46-Ps.18.47, not the span through web:Ps.18.48. Span not contested; the defect is the warrant's stated feature.

reviews.reasoning: The seam at web:Ps.18.48|web:Ps.18.49 is real and I support it on the bytes: oshb:Ps.18.50 = web:Ps.18.49 opens with the inferential עַל כֵּ֤ן, and the closing verse shifts to third-person royal reference, so the couplet is a genuine unit. Dual-cite arithmetic is not required by the refs as filed because the row cites 0 MT refs, and the selah note is true and span-scoped (no selah key in Ps 18 in pmarks_Ps.json). The device_notes correctly refuse the book-boundary reading — the Book I doxology is at MT 41.14 = web:Ps.41.13, not here. Two things I flag rather than file: the row's driver is a Hebrew lexical item (עַל כֵּ֤ן, a two-word compound rather than one particle) that is never quoted or dual-cited, which leaves the seam's own warrant argued entirely from English; and at two verses the row sits below the ~4-8 verse strophe norm, which is a unit-typology question for the form lens rather than mine. What I do file is a disclosure failure: the row quotes the verse carrying Ps 18's only ketiv/qere (1 note in 1 verse, pmarks_Ps.json), and the clause its dynastic warrant rests on is the one the qere produces. Confidence 'high' overstates a row whose closing evidence is undisclosed-variant-dependent.

challenges.claim: The row quotes web:Ps.18.50 = oshb:Ps.18.51 without disclosing that verse's ketiv/qere, although the clause its dynastic warrant rests on renders the qere.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries oshb:Ps.18.51 = web:Ps.18.50 with 1 note — the only ketiv/qere in Ps 18 (book-wide inventory: 68 notes over 65 verses; single-witness WLC/OSHB). The staged bytes hold the pair unpointed-then-pointed at the head of the verse: ketiv מגדל, qere מַגְדִּיל֮ (collate.py: byte tier at oshb:Ps.18.51 for both). WEB's “He gives great deliverance to his king” (web:Ps.18.50) follows the qere מַגְדִּיל֮ (hiphil participle); the ketiv מגדל is the nominal reading. The row quotes that clause and builds the third-person dynastic warrant on it while leaving the variant undisclosed. This is not a house convention in the cluster: the Ps 21 opening row discloses its ketiv/qere at oshb:Ps.21.2 = web:Ps.21.1. Selecting a reading is out of scope; disclosing that the quoted rendering rests on one is not.

reviews.reasoning: The seam at web:Ps.19.6|web:Ps.19.7 is well founded and the original-language work behind it holds: I re-derived all 4 of its substantive claims. The divine-name distribution is exactly as stated: a pointed byte sweep of אֵ֑ל returns 21 verses book-wide with Ps 19's only hit at oshb:Ps.19.2 = web:Ps.19.1, and Yahweh does not occur in oshb:Ps.19.2-Ps.19.7 = web:Ps.19.1-Ps.19.6 (0 occurrences across those 6 verses), the psalm's first Yahweh falling at oshb:Ps.19.8 = web:Ps.19.7. The row handles the short-token homography hazard correctly and explicitly, distinguishing אֵ֑ל from the negative אַֽל at oshb:Ps.19.14 = web:Ps.19.13 on pointed bytes rather than skeleton — which is the right call, since a skeleton sweep of אֵ֑ל returns 656 verses. Title handling follows the owner ruling (web:Ps.19.0 = oshb:Ps.19.1, is_counted_title true), all 3 dual-cites are arithmetically correct for a shift+1 psalm, all 4 WEB quotes are verbatim, and the selah note is true and span-scoped (0 occurrences in 6 verses). The one defect is that the row corroborates its count against an instrument that does not exist as described. I also note, without filing, that naming the toolkit script in row prose is apparatus leakage that the register rules disfavour.

challenges.claim: The row corroborates its zero-Yahweh count against 'sweep.py's book-wide Yahweh-lexeme index', an instrument that does not exist: the tool performs byte / accent-stripped / contiguous-consonantal substring sweeps and resolves no lexemes.
challenges.evidence: sweep.py returns verse hit-lists at three string tiers and documents itself as 'a contiguous consonantal SUBSTRING search, not a root/lemma search'; TOOLKIT.md warns that skeleton sweeps conflate homographs. The distinction is live in this very row: a skeleton sweep of the row's own אֵ֑ל returns 656 verses book-wide because the string matches inside unrelated words — it hits oshb:Ps.19.15 = web:Ps.19.14 through וְגֹאֲלִֽי and oshb:Ps.19.14 = web:Ps.19.13 through the negative אַֽל — whereas the pointed byte sweep of אֵ֑ל returns 21 verses, Ps 19's only hit being oshb:Ps.19.2 = web:Ps.19.1 (1 occurrence across the 6 verses of the span). The second corroborator the row names is real: psalm_device_inventory.json yhwh_elohim_per_psalm holds yhwh 7 for Ps 19. The counts reproduce exactly (0 occurrences in 6 verses), so only the named instrument is defective.

reviews.reasoning: The panel and its seam are right and the quantitative claim is exactly right — I re-derived it rather than inheriting it. A byte sweep of יְהוָ֣ה spliced from oshb:Ps.19.8 puts Ps 19's Yahweh at MT 19:8, 19:9, 19:10 and 19:15, i.e. web:Ps.19.7, web:Ps.19.8, web:Ps.19.9 and web:Ps.19.14 — 7 token-occurrences across 4 verses, matching psalm_device_inventory.json's yhwh 7 for the psalm and confirming that all seven fall inside this panel. The negative claim also holds: no Yahweh or El token occurs at oshb:Ps.19.12-Ps.19.14 = web:Ps.19.11-Ps.19.13. The quoted Hebrew collates at byte tier at its cited ref, all 4 WEB quotations at web:Ps.19.7, web:Ps.19.10, web:Ps.19.11 and web:Ps.19.14 are verbatim, and the synonym pairing described at web:Ps.19.7-Ps.19.9 is accurate. web:Ps.19.8 is argued in prose without a bare ref of its own, but it sits inside the row's own span and is exempt by design, so I do not file it. What I do file is the numbering-disclosure gap: two of the four MT verses carrying the headline count are cited bare in a shift+1 psalm.

challenges.claim: In a shift+1 psalm the row's headline sevenfold count rests on 2 of 4 MT verse citations — oshb:Ps.19.9 and oshb:Ps.19.10 — that appear nowhere with the mandated dual-cite arithmetic, while the same verses appear one number lower under WEB numbering in the rationale.
challenges.evidence: The signal reports 2 occurrences each at oshb:Ps.19.8, oshb:Ps.19.9 and oshb:Ps.19.10 and 1 at oshb:Ps.19.15; boundary_evidence_refs supply arithmetic for only 2 of 4 (oshb:Ps.19.8 = web:Ps.19.7 and oshb:Ps.19.15 = web:Ps.19.14). The missing arithmetic is oshb:Ps.19.9 = web:Ps.19.8 and oshb:Ps.19.10 = web:Ps.19.9 (Ps 19 is shift+1 in web_mt_offset_map.json, title = MT v1). The exposure is concrete rather than formal: the rationale lists the same four verses as web:Ps.19.7, Ps.19.8, Ps.19.9 and Ps.19.14, so the row presents 2 overlapping sets of the numerals 8 and 9 meaning different verses, and only 2 of 4 carry the crosswalk. The count itself re-derives exactly — a byte sweep of יְהוָ֣ה (spliced from oshb:Ps.19.8 = web:Ps.19.7) yields 7 token-occurrences across those 4 verses, matching the inventory's yhwh 7 for Ps 19 — so the defect is disclosure, not arithmetic. Note that citation_sweep.py's dual-cite arm iterates boundary_evidence_refs only, so the 2 of 4 prose-borne bare oshb: cites pass GREEN; the defect is real but tool-invisible.

reviews.reasoning: The span survives but its stated closing warrant does not. Ps 20 at 9 WEB verses is above the short-psalm threshold, so a two-row split is policy-compliant, and the rejected_alternative reaches for the right tier-1 driver — the עַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי pivot at oshb:Ps.20.7 = web:Ps.20.6 — which is what actually fixes the seam at web:Ps.20.5|web:Ps.20.6. The selah handling is correct and corroborative only: pmarks_Ps.json carries selah at oshb:Ps.20.4 = web:Ps.20.3 (1 occurrence, the psalm's only one across its 9 verses), verse_map_web has web_selah true there, the WEB quotation includes “Selah.” as verse text, and the row does not rest the seam on it. The title dual-cite and is_counted_title claim both verify. The poetry_lines figures cited from verse_map_web are numerically accurate, though line-layout is modern typesetting and carries no evidential weight. The failure is the sentence that states where the unit ends: it locates a cohortative communal vow one verse before it occurs, and in doing so argues for a span the row does not declare. Confidence 'high' is not supportable while the closing warrant is wrong.

challenges.claim: The closing warrant misplaces the mood shift and contradicts the row's own span: it says the unit 'ends where the verb mood shifts from jussive petition to cohortative communal vow at web:Ps.20.4', but web:Ps.20.4 is still jussive petition and the 1cp cohortative falls at web:Ps.20.5 — inside the span, one verse before its end.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.20.5 = web:Ps.20.4 reads יִֽתֶּן לְךָ֥ כִלְבָבֶ֑ךָ וְֽכָל עֲצָתְךָ֥ יְמַלֵּֽא (collate.py: byte tier) — 3ms in 2 of 2 finite verbs, rendered “May he grant you your heart’s desire, and fulfill all your counsel.” (web:Ps.20.4); there is no 1cp form in it. The cohortatives are the verse after: נְרַנְּנָ֤ה and נִדְגֹּ֑ל at oshb:Ps.20.6 = web:Ps.20.5 (byte tier), rendered “We will triumph in your salvation. In the name of our God, we will set up our banners.” (web:Ps.20.5). So the shift the row names as its terminus occurs inside the span, and on the row's own reasoning the unit would have to end at web:Ps.20.3 rather than at the declared web:Ps.20.5. The seam itself is sound on the row's other warrant, the עַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי pivot at oshb:Ps.20.7 = web:Ps.20.6, so the span is not contested — the replacement warrant must pass the test that kills this one, in the same edit.

reviews.reasoning: Clean row; nothing here rises to a challenge. All 4 dual-cites are arithmetically correct for shift+1 and are the cluster's tidiest set (web:Ps.20.6 = oshb:Ps.20.7, web:Ps.20.7 = oshb:Ps.20.8, web:Ps.20.8 = oshb:Ps.20.9, web:Ps.20.9 = oshb:Ps.20.10, all 4 verified against web_mt_offset_map.json). All 4 WEB quotations are verbatim against verse_map_web. The selah absence claim is correctly span-scoped and true: pmarks_Ps.json holds exactly one selah key in Ps 20, at oshb:Ps.20.4 = web:Ps.20.3, hence 0 occurrences in oshb:Ps.20.7-Ps.20.10 as the row states. The person-shift signal verifies on the bytes: יָדַ֗עְתִּי is 1cs at oshb:Ps.20.7 = web:Ps.20.6, and the 1cp וַאֲנַ֓חְנוּ and וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ open the cola at oshb:Ps.20.8 = web:Ps.20.7 and oshb:Ps.20.9 = web:Ps.20.8. The closing 'imperative cry' is accurate — הוֹשִׁ֑יעָה at oshb:Ps.20.10 = web:Ps.20.9 is a hiphil imperative. One observation that does not affect the verdict: the argument leans on WEB's “but we trust in the name of Yahweh our God” (web:Ps.20.7), where 'trust' is supplied — the MT colon has no verb of trusting, opening on וַאֲנַ֓חְנוּ and closing on a verb of invoking — but the row's actual load-bearing point is the 1cp voice, which is present in the bytes, and the English is properly quoted as WEB. Confidence 'high' is calibrated.

The span and the seam are right and the original-language work behind them is careful. The second-person claim verifies exactly as scoped: 2ms address runs from oshb:Ps.21.2 = web:Ps.21.1 through oshb:Ps.21.7 = web:Ps.21.6 and breaks at oshb:Ps.21.8 = web:Ps.21.7, where יִשְׂמַח's subject gives way to third-person reference to the king — so 'runs web:Ps.21.1-Ps.21.6' with a third-person hinge at web:Ps.21.7 is precisely stated. The selah citation is correct and is used to reject a split rather than to drive one: pmarks_Ps.json has selah at oshb:Ps.21.3 = web:Ps.21.2 (1 occurrence), matching web_selah in verse_map_web. The ketiv/qere disclosure is present, correctly located and correctly counted against the inventory (1 note at oshb:Ps.21.2 = web:Ps.21.1), and the row is right that it does not touch the strength-word — I note that the verse has 2 verbs that WEB renders with 'rejoices' and that the variant attaches to the second (יגיל ketiv / יָּ֥גֶל qere), so 'the verb rendered rejoices' under-identifies which word is affected; that is a precision observation, not a filed defect. What I file is a positional claim about the Hebrew that the bytes contradict.

challenges.claim: 'the Hebrew opens on the root behind “your strength”' is contradicted by the bytes — oshb:Ps.21.2 = web:Ps.21.1 opens on the divine name, with the quoted form second — and it conflates an inflected form with a root.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.21.2 = web:Ps.21.1 opens יְֽהוָ֗ה בְּעָזְּךָ֥ יִשְׂמַח (collate.py: byte tier for all 3 tokens at that ref); what is verse-initial is יְֽהוָ֗ה, not בְּעָזְּךָ֥. The quoted item is also not a root but a fully inflected form — preposition prefix, noun, 2ms suffix — which matters because the neighbouring row counts on this string. The fronting the row is reaching for is genuine, since בְּעָזְּךָ֥ does precede the verb יִשְׂמַח, so the defect is one of statement rather than of substance: the accurate observation is that the psalm opens on the divine name and fronts the strength-phrase before its verb, which also strengthens the bracket with oshb:Ps.21.14 = web:Ps.21.13, where יְֽהוָ֗ה's counterpart and בְּעֻזֶּ֑ךָ recur together.

reviews.reasoning: The span is right, the inclusio is real, and the row's honesty about what the bytes do not settle is a genuine strength: the addressee across web:Ps.21.8-Ps.21.12 really is unresolved, since 2ms verbs run through the section while Yahweh is referred to in the third person at oshb:Ps.21.10 = web:Ps.21.9, and the row records this as unsettled rather than resolving it — with confidence 'medium', which is correctly calibrated for that. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier at their cited refs, both dual-cites are arithmetically correct for shift+1, the WEB quotations at web:Ps.21.8 and web:Ps.21.13 are verbatim (2 of 2 checked), and the numeric result of the sweep is exactly right. The defect is in how the sweep is reported: the 3 verses it reports are right but its object is never named, it is labelled a root when what produces the figure is an inflected skeleton, its third verse is left unidentified, and the repetition claim is made without naming the tier at which the two forms actually agree.

challenges.claim: The sweep's object is never named and is mislabelled a root — the figure '3 verses book-wide' comes from the inflected skeleton shared by the two quoted forms, not from the root — and the accompanying repetition claim omits the tier at which the two forms agree.
challenges.evidence: Both quoted forms reduce to one skeleton, and sweep.py --skel on it returns 3 verses book-wide, 3 token-occurrences: oshb:Ps.21.2 = web:Ps.21.1, oshb:Ps.21.14 = web:Ps.21.13, and oshb:Ps.74.13 = web:Ps.74.13 (identity psalm) — so the row's arithmetic and its unit are right and the unnamed third verse is Ps 74:13. The object matters because a root-level claim would not yield 3: what was swept is a prefixed, suffixed form-skeleton, and the row calls it 'the strength-root string' without stating the string. The tier matters for the same reason: בְּעָזְּךָ֥ byte-matches only oshb:Ps.21.2 and בְּעֻזֶּ֑ךָ byte-matches only oshb:Ps.21.14, and each is unique to its own verse at accent-stripped tier as well (1 verse each), so the two are identical only at skeleton tier. 'Repeats the same strength-root' is therefore safe only as a skeleton-tier statement and must say so.
